summary: The article argues that Community Learning Centers (CLCs) are extending education beyond the classroom by partnering with local businesses, non-profits, banks and civic groups. It describes example partnerships in tech education, apprenticeships, financial literacy, entrepreneurship and adult upskilling, and cites a study of economic returns. It also stresses equity for disadvantaged students and youth involvement in shaping CLC programs.
one_line: Community Learning Centers use partnerships with local businesses, non-profits and civic groups to enrich learning, promote equity and drive economic growth.
key_facts: Regina Hall is Director of the Springfield Innovative Learning Hub, which opened on October 5, 2023.
Dr. Miles Peterson, an educational consultant, says community partnerships can turn CLCs into 'bustling nodes of knowledge, technology, and cultural exchange.'
Wilmington Waves, a technology start-up, partnered with the Harbor Community Learning Space (established November 12, 2023) to give learners hands-on tech education and create a talent pipeline.

A study released January 15, 2024 by the National Economic Council on Education (NECE) found communities saw a return of one dollar and sixty cents within the first year for every dollar invested in collaborative educational efforts.
Johnson's Engineering partnered with Midtown Vocational Center on February 28, 2024 and reported a 20% increase in productivity from apprenticeship programs sourced from the CLC.
East Side Learning Initiative began collaborating with community-based organizations on March 10, 2024 to support socio-economically disadvantaged students.
Emily García, program director at East Side Learning Initiative, said 'Each local partnership brings us closer to leveling the educational playing field.'
Greene County Savings Bank facilitated a financial literacy workshop at the Riverdale CLC on September 20, 2023.

The Cedar Town Learning Collective and the Cedar Town Chamber of Commerce launched an entrepreneurship incubator on December 1, 2023, which has since produced five successful community-based startups.
Lakeside Learning Community joined Blue Ridge Manufacturing on October 25, 2023 to offer evening courses in advanced manufacturing techniques.
The article says involving youth in developing CLC initiatives keeps programs current with the needs of the future workforce.
